scenario: A real local Next dev server receives an authenticated Studio POST /api/studio/videos/:id/publish for a synthetic ready SELF_HLS video and subscriber.
The committed publication and NEW_VIDEO_FANOUT intent are verified in PostgreSQL; a disposable test trigger gives the new job a future lease so the immediate best-effort kick cannot consume it.
The publishing server process group is SIGKILLed after the committed HTTP response, then the test trigger is removed and the durable job lease is released.
A fresh local Next dev server starts and the real authenticated GET /api/cron/premiere-notifications endpoint claims and completes the persisted fan-out job.
The subscriber receives exactly one NEW_VIDEO notification; a repeated real cron HTTP request leaves the count at one.

vitest.command: DATABASE_URL=<disposable> DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED=<disposable> npx vitest run --config vitest.postgres.config.ts tests/postgres/k23-publish-crash-cron-http.pg.test.ts

scope_limits: The crash boundary is after the successful publishing HTTP response; the trigger deterministically prevents the background fan-out kick from consuming the durable intent before the process group is killed.
The HLS asset, playback route, subscriber, and database rows are synthetic; there is no external R2/S3, production data, deployed cron scheduler, or independent review.

This proves recovery through the real local cron HTTP handler after process loss and retry idempotency for this publication path; K23 remains partial pending independent review and remaining premiere/provider boundaries.
